title: A Light for Thornwold
description: Thornwold's beacon has been dark since the Snuffing, and while it is, no lane runs on toward Cindermoor. The cart road from the landing used to run straight up to it.

stages.text: Bram Kettle says a bramble wall grew across the old cart road to the beacon in a single night, and the road behind it goes somewhere else every morning. Look at it for yourself, north of the lumber camp.

The cart road runs straight in under the brambles and doesn't come out, and a cutter's 'this way home' notch points into the thorns. Bram's cutters won't go in. Your ember leans toward the canes. Find a way past the wall to Thornwold's beacon.
Past the brambles the cart road runs straight on north into the Greying. Lanterns hang on some of the Keepers' waymarks, off the road to the west. Follow the lights, not the road.

Hob Marl, a collier in the clearing past the wall, says the road goes where the lanterns are, and the lanterns are hung by 'the Lamp', who comes along the ridge at dusk. The beacon is up on the ridge. The Keepers' stair climbs the north bank from the clearing.

The Lamp, at the lantern bench by the keeper's lodge, is Thornwold's beacon-keeper. The Ridge Light stands cold beside the lodge, and like the Gull's Beacon it will want a memory to burn. Learn what Thornwold can spare. (Thornwold's burning is still being written.)
